newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 3.78 pct up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 3.78 pct up on technical rebound.

text.p: Thai stocks rallied strongly on a technical rebound from a 48-point decline in the composite index last week amid talks that the authorities may introduce market support measures later this week, brokers said on Tuesday.
The SET index ended 29.88 points, or 3.78 percent, higher at 820.11 on moderate 5.06 billion baht turnover.

"Market sentiment improved on investor hopes that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) may issue measures to help the market when it meets on Thursday," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
Brokers said investors speculated that the Thai SEC may come up with medium and long-term measures to boost the market which lost 35 percent in 1996.
Brokers said the market welcomed Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan's announcement on Tuesday that he would cut annual government budget by at least 50 billion baht a year in fiscal year 1997 and 1998.

Morgan Stanley global strategy chief Barton Biggs said Asian markets, including Thailand, South Korea and India, could rally 30-35 percent in 1997 on any sharp correction of U.S. stock markets this year.
Thai stocks rallied across the board with the finance sector leading the gains rising 8.83 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising three baht to 190, Siam Cement rose 16 to 764, and National Finance advanced 4.25 to 47.25.
